title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
one_line_claim: StreamingLLM enables language models to handle long contexts by preserving initial tokens as attention sinks while using a sliding window for KV-cache compression.
method_summary: Combines attention sinks (preserving KV of initial tokens) with sliding-window attention to compress KV cache. Uses a fixed-size window of recent tokens plus initial tokens that naturally attract high attention, enabling generalization to long sequences without retraining. Optionally adds a placeholder token during pre-training as a dedicated sink.

key_findings.finding: Attention sink phenomenon allows recovery of window-attention performance by retaining initial-token KV.
key_findings.quote: keeping the KV of initial tokens will largely recover the performance of window attention

key_findings.finding: Enables Llama-2, MPT, Falcon, and Pythia to process up to 4 million tokens without fine-tuning.
key_findings.quote: perform stable and efficient language modeling with up to 4 million tokens and more

key_findings.finding: Achieves 22.2x speedup compared to sliding-window recomputation baselines.
key_findings.quote: StreamingLLM outperforms the sliding window recomputation baseline by up to 22.2x speedup

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression for long-context LLM inference. StreamingLLM is one of the compression methods HERALD evaluates.
differs_on: StreamingLLM provides lossless long-context inference; HERALD predicts when compression methods catastrophically fail.
StreamingLLM focuses on performance-stability trade-offs; HERALD detects specific failure modes (looping, non-termination).
StreamingLLM operates at design level; HERALD monitors per-token logit signals at inference time.
